# Results — Study 813 (Maximum-Drawdown Anomaly)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: sort a
cross-section on each name's **trailing 12-month maximum drawdown** (largest peak-to-trough
decline of cumulative total return); do the recently distressed (deep-drawdown) names
subsequently **under-earn** (distress) or **rebound**? We take no prior on the sign and stamp
what the tape shows. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

*Data stamp line: as-of 2026-06-30 · Fingerprint `357fd262912f` · 50 names · 3,895 spread days.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-252-day maximum drawdown** — the deepest peak-to-trough decline of the cumulative total-return price inside the window (positive magnitude, vectorised via a sliding-window running peak), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the bottom 30%** (shallow drawdown, *calm*), **short the top 30%** (deep drawdown, *distressed*), equal-weight; `spread = calm − distressed` |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled calm-vs-distressed books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a two-era cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. This bites a
drawdown study especially hard: the deepest drawdowns of all — the names that fell and never
recovered (bankruptcies, de-ratings) — are exactly the ones a survivor panel deletes, so the
observed distressed leg is a *survivor's* distress, milder than the true cross-section.

## The headline — long-calm / short-distressed spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% (calm) minus top-30% (distressed) trailing-MaxDD spread
(n = **3,895** days, median 50 names/day):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (calm − distressed)** | **−4.35 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−2.36** |
| one-sample *t* | −2.34 |
| calm book / distressed book | +5.34 bps / +9.68 bps (Welch *t* = −1.50) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.59 |

The **negative** sign is the whole story: `spread = calm − distressed` is significantly
negative, which means the **distressed** (deep-drawdown) names *out-earned* the calm ones. So
on this mega-cap tape the answer is **rebound, not distress** — a drawdown **reversal**. This is
one of the two outcomes the claim entertained; the desk simply reports which way it broke.

## Placebo — is the (reversal) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-MaxDD sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−4.35 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.046 bps (1.049) |
| position of observed | ≈ **4.19σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 1.000 ⇒ left-tail p ≈ 0.000) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −4.35 bps sits far in the **left** tail, so
the rebound is a real feature of the sort, not a chance alignment.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,761) | −2.41 bps | **−1.10** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −5.94 bps | **−2.09** |

**Not robust.** The rebound is entirely a 2018–2026 phenomenon; the 2010–2017 half is the same
sign but insignificant (*t* = −1.10). The pooled |t| ≥ 2 rests on one era — the decisive reason
this stamps **Weak**, not **Real**.

## The timer — can you get paid for it (either direction)?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| book | one-way cost | net/day | *t* (net) |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| specified (long calm / short distressed) | 1 bp | **−6.48 bps** | −3.49 |
| specified | 5 bps | **−14.48 bps** | −7.79 |
| **sign-flipped rebound** (long distressed / short calm) | 1 bp | **+2.21 bps** | +1.19 |
| sign-flipped rebound | 5 bps | **−5.79 bps** | −3.11 |

The specified book loses money outright. Even the *profitable* rebound direction earns only
+2.21 bps/day net at a **fantasy 1 bp** cost — and at *t* = +1.19 that is **not** statistically
significant — then goes negative by 5 bps. No paycheck either way. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "fragility" that deepens each name's
drawdown (higher vol + larger de-meaned downside jumps) and (with `edge>0`) depresses its
forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.53** (sd 1.07), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.004`, seed 813) | **+9.03** (Welch *t* = +9.18) |

The detector recovers a *planted distress* relation cleanly (deep drawdown → low forward return
→ **positive** calm-minus-distressed spread) and is quiet on the null — so the negative
real-tape sign is a genuine rebound on this universe, not a bug. *(A faithful-engine / power
check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Sorting on the trailing 12-month maximum drawdown, the long-calm /
  short-distressed spread is **−4.35 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−2.36**): the distressed names
  **out-earned** — a **drawdown reversal**, one of the two outcomes the claim entertained, and
  the placebo confirms it is not a lucky sort (≈4.2σ into the left tail). But it is **not robust
  across eras** (*t* = −1.10 in 2010–2017 vs −2.09 in 2018–2026), so it clears the pooled |t| ≥ 2
  bar only marginally and on one half of the sample — Weak, not Real. Survivorship biases the
  magnitude (permanent losers absent).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified book loses money (−6.48 bps/day net at 1 bp); the
  profitable rebound direction earns +2.21 bps/day net at a fantasy 1 bp (*t* = +1.19, not
  significant) and turns negative by 5 bps.
